text: just seen a guy order in french at a bakery counter. no google translate. no phrasebook. no duolingo. no notes app vocab list. two years of school textbooks and pure nerve against an entire country. the queue went silent. Absolute lunatic behaviour
base_video: Creator sitting outside a cafe holding a coffee, looking off to the side at someone out of frame, then a slow blinking double take straight down the lens. No talking.
audio: original audio, room tone with faint street noise
caption: would you have risked it or pointed at the croissant
why_this_brand: The bakery-counter freeze after years of school French is the exact language-learner moment Duolingo users joke about.
what_changed: Removed the line 'he said a full sentence out loud.' so the escalation runs straight into the silent queue and the verdict.

format.reason: Duolingo is an app with no physical demo and a very relatable old way: five years of school French and still freezing at a Paris bakery counter, which lands hardest as a silent reaction to a block of text. The meme-literate, self-aware tone is exactly what this format rewards, and the streak anxiety angle is a built-in comment trigger without needing any footage from the brand.
format.why_not_runner_up: A language app has nothing visual to carousel through, so slides would just be text on images doing the same job with weaker hold in the first 1.5 seconds.

editor_fix: cut 'he said a full sentence out loud.' so the escalation runs straight into the queue going silent and then the verdict.
